purpose: Primary-source context for final experimental interpretation; not coursework prose or slides.

sources.title: When Does Generating More Help?
verified_facts: Uses matched q*r training-example buckets, not a common priced acquisition wallet.
Collects up to 32 correct responses per question; same training epochs and three repeated training seeds.
Small-budget source expansion and repeated response generation can be comparable; source expansion becomes stronger at larger budgets.
sources.scope_for_our_study: A small-budget non-difference does not refute its findings. Our separate problem price and failed-attempt tariff target a different resource constraint.

sources.title: OpenMathInstruct-2
verified_facts: At 256K pairs, varying unique questions from 1K to 6.5K favors more questions in that MATH validation setting.
sources.scope_for_our_study: Direct prior P/R allocation evidence; substantially larger inventory and more answers per question than our finite study. No claim that studying breadth versus depth is itself new.

sources.title: DART-Math
verified_facts: Studies one-response coverage and synthesis attempts under a maximum per-query attempt limit.
Explicitly reports the tradeoff between achieving response quotas and total raw sampling cost.
Notes that sample count alone is not a fair cost comparison across different generators.
sources.scope_for_our_study: Failed attempts and difficult-parent generation costs have prior treatment. Use one teacher and distinguish hypothetical prices, token tariffs, hardware time and invoices.

novelty_claim: Not established by these preliminary experiments; decisions require validation across procurement traces and a stated cost model.
